Jordan —

Great questions. Short answer up front: for a time-sensitive pilot where you want predictable invoicing + the ability to leverage cloud co-sell incentives, we usually recommend one of two lanes depending on your priorities: 

1) Marketplace private offer (AWS/Azure/GCP private offers) — if you need quick procurement and want cloud billing consolidation. Pros: fast issuance of a private offer, can appear on your cloud invoice, and preserves co-sell eligibility in many cases. Cons: invoicing cadence and tax treatment tied to the cloud provider; some enterprise PO workflows prefer vendor invoice.

2) Direct MSA + vendor invoice — if you need Redwood to produce a vendor invoice (for PO matching) and require specific contractual language (data residency, audit access, custom SLA). Pros: full control over invoice and contract terms; easier for finance to reconcile with PO. Cons: slightly longer legal lead time (MSA + SOW).

Key notes: 
- Co-sell credits: AWS co-sell typically requires a partner-registered deal and sometimes a private offer route to flow incentives. We can engage our partner sales rep to register the opportunity simultaneously with the private offer. We will include that step in the mutual action plan.
- Timeline: If you want a purchase by Oct 10, private offer is generally faster (we can get a private offer issued within ~5 business days once terms are agreed). Direct MSA + first vendor invoice can also hit your timeline if you agree on standard MSA language quickly — we have a short-form MSA template for pilots.
- Legal / security flags: data residency and audit logs are supported in our Dedicated/Private deployment options; hosted API is multiregional — we should capture required controls in the SOW. We will also provide SOC 2 documentation and network diagrams on request.

I've attached a short comparison matrix and a tentative TCO spreadsheet for the three lanes. Next steps I recommend: 
1) Pick preferred path (private offer or vendor invoice) by Fri 9/10 so we can start paperwork.
2) If private offer, we will draft a private offer quote and loop in our cloud partner contact.
3) If vendor invoice, we'll share the short-form pilot MSA and a sample invoice template.

Looping in Vanessa to coordinate partner contacts and Karthik on pricing/discounts.

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart

Hi Jordan — appreciate the clarifying questions. Quick practical answers below, plus a recommended execution plan.

1) Vendor invoice vs AWS invoice:
- AWS Marketplace (standard listing): AWS invoices Acme; Redwood receives payment from AWS. In that flow, AWS is the billing party. Many finance teams require a vendor invoice they can PO-match; in that case you can use AWS invoice with a copy of the private offer + AWS supporting docs.
- AWS Marketplace (Private Offer): still billed via AWS but the private offer flow lets us set negotiated pricing and term. In many cases, customers accept AWS invoice + private offer as sufficient for PO matching. If your policy mandates a Redwood-issued vendor invoice, the direct MSA route is the only guaranteed path.

2) Co-sell credits and partner registration:
- Private offers often map cleanly to co-sell registration; we register the opportunity with our AWS partner rep and supply required worksheets. With a direct MSA, we can still register the opportunity but eligibility for certain cloud incentives (e.g., AWS ISV Accelerate credits) may depend on the marketplace/private offer being used. We will coordinate with our partner manager to maximize credit capture regardless of route.

3) Timing (typical):
- Private Offer (AWS): 3–7 business days from agreement to private offer issuance; invoice on your AWS billing cycle (monthly).
- Direct MSA (vendor invoice): 5–10 business days to finalize short-form pilot MSA + generate first invoice (immediate invoice delivery once purchase order is received).

Recommended execution plan for your case (pilot by Oct 10):
A) If Acme requires vendor invoice for PO matching and cannot accept AWS invoice, choose direct MSA with short pilot addendum. We’ll expedite legal — we have a pilot addendum template that focuses only on term, pilot scope, and invoice flow.
B) If Acme can accept AWS invoice + private offer docs for PO matching, choose private offer now. We will:
   - Prepare private offer quote and register the opportunity with AWS partner team (1 business day).
   - Have you approve pricing/term (1–2 business days).
   - AWS issues private offer (3–5 business days).

Attachments: I re-attached the comparison and added an estimated TCO by route. Also included a sample pilot addendum and a sample vendor invoice template so your finance team can see layout.

Next steps: Jordan — can you confirm by Fri 9/10 whether Acme can accept AWS invoice + private offer docs? If yes, we'll start private offer drafting immediately and loop in our partner manager. If no, we will start the short MSA cadence and route an expedited DocuSign envelope.

Thanks —
